manual_insights.title: 📢 NEET Results Published — Key Takeaways
manual_insights.content:
According to the latest **GMA Insight Review**, this year's results are highly competitive.

Based on preliminary data analysis, we predict the safe cutoff for Government Medical Colleges will rise to **~600 marks** on an All-India basis. Students in the borderline range should strategically include aided and self-financing options in their choice filling to maximize their chances.

manual_insights.title: 🎓 Kerala Rank Insight
manual_insights.content:
**State Rank 1 – 2,000**
You have a very strong chance of securing a seat in a **Government Medical College**. Focus on prioritizing top colleges based on infrastructure and clinical exposure.

**State Rank 2,000 – 5,000**
Prioritize government colleges first, but strategically keep reputed aided and self-financing (private) colleges as solid backup options.

**State Rank 5,000 – 10,000**
Include all government colleges in your preference list, but you must explore private colleges to ensure you don't miss out on an allotment.

**State Rank Above 10,000**
Keep a broad choice list consisting mostly of private and self-financing institutions. If you hold a minority or category reservation certificate, ensure it is validated during registration to open up additional seat matrices.

> 💡 **Golden Rule:** Always order your choices based on your **true preference**, not just the previous year's cutoff order. Place your dream colleges first, followed by realistic backups.

manual_insights.title: ⚠️ Kerala CEE Critical Admission Rules
manual_insights.content:
**1. Mandatory Physical Joining**
The candidate who gets an admission in Round 1 must join physically in the allotted college to participate in the next round. Anyone who fails to take admission will be eliminated and cannot participate in further rounds.

**2. No New Choices After Round 1**
Check closely when making your choice list! Students cannot add new colleges after the first allotment. Your only option in subsequent rounds is to swap or rearrange the order of your existing choices.

manual_insights.title: 🎓 Karnataka Rank Insight
manual_insights.content:
**State Rank 1 – 3,000**
You have excellent chances for top **Government Medical Colleges** like BMCRI and MMCRI. Lock your top preferences securely.

**State Rank 3,000 – 15,000**
Include newer government colleges and top private medical colleges in your preference list. KEA counselling allows for smooth upgradation in Round 2, so fill choices expansively.

**State Rank Above 15,000**
Focus heavily on private medical colleges (GMP/OPN quotas). If you hold any special category or linguistic minority certificates, ensure they are verified by KEA to access specialized seat matrices.

> 💡 **Golden Rule:** KEA choice filling is a one-time process for Round 1 and Round 2. Add as many choices as possible in Round 1 itself; you cannot add new choices in Round 2 unless new colleges are added.

manual_insights.title: ❓ Commonly Asked Questions (FAQ)
manual_insights.content:
**Q: What if I get a seat in Kerala and Karnataka at the same time?**
You can take part in more than one counselling if you're eligible for each, but you can only study at one college. You can't keep both seats for long, because joining means paying the fee and handing over your original certificates. Your originals can only be in one place.

**What to do:**
1. Decide which seat you actually prefer (college, cost, distance, bond) before either deadline.
2. Check the exit rules in both prospectuses. Leaving a seat after joining can mean losing the fee you paid, paying a penalty, or being barred from later rounds.
3. If one counselling is still running, think about timing. Joining one seat may stop you from taking part in the other's later rounds.
4. Never leave a seat unreported "just in case" without asking first. Seat blocking is penalised.

**Q: Should I register for both Kerala counselling and All India (MCC) counselling?**
Yes, if you're eligible. Kerala CEE handles the state quota, management and NRI seats in Kerala. MCC handles the 15% All India Quota in government colleges and deemed universities across India. Each has its own portal, fee, option list and deadlines, so registering for both gives you more chances.

**Q: I got an All India Quota seat. Can I still take part in Kerala counselling?**
Often yes in the early rounds, but it depends on the round and whether you've joined and frozen the AIQ seat. Joining a seat in a later MCC round may end your eligibility for further rounds elsewhere. Check the current MCC bulletin and Kerala prospectus before you join or resign anything.

**Q: What's the difference between state quota and All India Quota?**
In government medical colleges, 85% of seats go to the state's own candidates through state counselling, using the Kerala rank. The other 15% go to students from anywhere in India through MCC, using the All India Rank. The same college can be easier to get through one quota than the other.

**Q: What happens if I don't pay the fee or report on time?**
Your allotment is usually cancelled. In Kerala counselling, you also lose the higher options you were waiting for. Don't leave payment to the last day, as portals slow down near deadlines.

**Q: I got a seat in Round 1 but I want a better college. What do I do?**
Secure the seat you have first by paying and reporting as required. Then keep only the higher options you'd genuinely prefer; if one comes through in the next round, you'll be moved. Remove any higher option you wouldn't actually take, because if it's allotted you lose your current seat.

**Q: Can I change my option list after submitting it?**
Usually you can edit options until the option entry window closes. Kerala counselling generally opens a window before later rounds to delete or rearrange options. You typically can't add new colleges once a round has started, so check the notice for each round.

**Q: What are the mop-up round and the stray vacancy round?**
These are the last rounds, held to fill seats left vacant after the main rounds. Cutoffs are often more relaxed, but eligibility is stricter: students who already joined a seat may not be allowed to take part. Keep your originals and fee ready, because you may have to report within a day or two.

**Q: I'm from Kerala but studied Class 12 outside Kerala. Can I get state quota?**
Kerala decides eligibility by Keralite status (your nativity), not where you studied. Keralites who studied outside the state are generally eligible, but you'll need proof of nativity and may need a migration certificate. Check the eligibility section of the current prospectus.

**Q: My non-creamy layer or community certificate has a mistake or has expired. What now?**
Apply for a fresh one from the village office or Tahsildar immediately. Certificates usually need to be valid on a date fixed in the prospectus. A claim without a valid certificate can be rejected, moving you to the general list, so don't wait for allotment to fix this.

manual_insights.title: 📋 KEAM 2026 Allotment: Document Checklist
manual_insights.content:
Congratulations on your allotment! 🎉 You **must report to your allotted college** within the joining deadline to secure your seat. Bring the following documents in **original**:

1. Data Sheet of KEAM 2026
2. Allotment Memo of this phase
3. Certificate to prove date of birth
4. Transfer Certificate from the Institution last attended and Conduct Certificate
5. Original mark list of Higher Secondary or equivalent
6. NEET(UG)-2026/NATA-2026 Score Card, if applicable
7. Migration Certificate, if applicable
8. Receipt of fee remitted by Online payment
9. Eligibility certificate from the University concerned (for candidates who passed from boards other than Kerala HSE/VHSE, CBSE, or CISCE)
10. Physical Fitness Certificate in the relevant format given in Annexure XVII of the Prospectus
11. Originals of all the documents/certificates uploaded during the online application
12. Any other documents required in the allotment as per notification

> ⚠️ **Important:** Failure to report within the deadline will result in **cancellation of your allotment**. Carry all originals!
